To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of deep learning for the association metric improves the performance of the SORT framework, that the use of appearance information reduces the number of identity switch errors by 45%, and that the use of the SORT framework in combination with a deep association model allows to track multiple objects in real-time.
1. We propose a novel approach for multiple object tracking that integrates appearance features into the SORT framework.

1) SORT is a simple and efficient tracking framework that achieves state of the art performance on the MOTChallenge 2) We propose an efficient extension to SORT that integrates appearance information to reduce the number of track switches 3) The extension reduces the number of switches by 45%, while still maintaining the simplicity of the original framework 4) The proposed framework is able to track objects at high frame rates and achieves competitive performance on the MOT2015 dataset
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How can we effectively combine visual appearance and motion information to reduce identity switches? What is the computational cost of such a system? Can we achieve competitive performance at high framerates?
